To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the weakly-coupling regime of QCD: (i) the favoured pairing channel for each flavour is CSL when the three flavours self-paired; and (ii) the favoured pairing channels for the up and down flavours are CSL and for the strange flavour is polar when the up and the down flavours undergo 2SC.

in the 3SC phase the favoured single-flavour pairing pattern of all three flavours is colour-spin- locked (CSL) pseudoscalar pairing, and that in the 2SC+CSL phase the favoured pairing pattern of the self-paired strange quarks is a 'polarized' state that breaks rotational symmetry.

the favoured pairing pattern of single-flavour pairing in the three-flavour colour-superconductivity phase depends on whether all three flavours self pair or whether two flavours pair with themselves and one flavour pairs with the other two flavours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
pairing of quarks in three-flavour matter, and the effects of the induced colour chemical potential on the favoured pairing channels.
the pairing of three-flavour quarks at finite temperature and chemical potential, and the resulting colour-superconductivity in the quark matter of neutron stars.
pairing of quarks in three-flavour colour superconductivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CSL phase is not the favoured pairing state of quark matter at weak coupling, but that this statement depends crucially on whether the quarks self-pair or pair with each other.
the 2SC+CSL phase is preferred to the 2SC+polar phase, and the CSL phase is preferred to all others.
in the weakly-coupling limit, 2SC pairing is the favoured phase for quark matter at low densities, while the favoured phase at high densities is a polar colour-spin-locked phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the favoured single-flavour pairing phase in three-flavour colour superconductivity is the CSL phase, but that it may be unstable to a polar phase when the up and/or down quarks undergo two-flavour pairing.
the 2SC pairing scenario is favoured over the single-flavour pairing scenario for the case of three-flavour quarks.
the 2SC+CSL scenario is favoured for the bulk of the phase diagram of quark matter in the weak-coupling regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2SC phase is not necessarily a precursor to the self-pairing phase, and that self-pairing phases may be more common than previously thought.

the 2SC+strange phase has lower free energy than the 2SC phase at all densities, and so should be preferred over the latter in any astrophysical setting where the 2SC is a candidate for the ground state.
the phase structure of three-flavour quarks depends sensitively on the pairing channel of the up and down flavours.
